title: Alfred Williams and single-head snare drums
summary: He saw Alfred Williams only in parades and funerals, and describes the single-head snare drum.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Yeah, that's a tom-tom. Yeah. You call it tom-tom. Mm-hmm. That's it. Uh, let's see. What else we got here? Uh, uh, you've always, you know, you didn't start on right or something, you just, uh, carried on playing from left, I mean, right from the start, say, left foot and left hand. Yeah. That's where I first started out. Yeah. Uh, what do you remember of Alfred Williams in the early days? Can you remember how you played the tom?
Well, most of the time that I saw Alfred Williams, he was playing parades or funerals.
I've never, uh, as yet, as long as I've been knowing him, I've never seen him play at parties or dance or anything like that, so I couldn't tell you how he played.
Uh, how about these, uh, single head snare drums?
Well, I never did use none of them.
How would they be a single head snare drum?
Well, it's made like a banjo. Yeah. You know, it's a single head with no bottom. Where would the snares be? The snares would be right up on the top. Oh, underneath the...

Well, I'd say you turned an ordinary snare drum up and was beating on the snare head. Yeah, that's right, that's right, that's right. Oh, yeah, I get you. Of course, a lot of the fellas would use that. John McMurray probably used that, didn't they?
